title: SCIM atomic joiner: safe user-to-group linkage, repair workflows, and audit handoff
creator: Lena Brooks
description:
Summary:
Implement an "atomic joiner" pattern for SCIM provisioning that guarantees user-to-group linkage is durable, idempotent, and repairable across concurrent delta events and transient downstream failures. This ticket focuses on the server-side orchestration, the repair/playbook, and the audit handoff so admins can reconcile mismatches without manual user recreation.

Background:
We get intermittent customer reports of users present in the IdP but missing group links in Redwood (or vice-versa) after bursts of SCIM updates from some enterprise IdPs. Root causes include: parallel group-membership writes, partial failures during group update, and eventual-consistency races with background reconciliation. Existing retry strategies help, but we need a stronger transactional approach for join operations plus a clear repair workflow and anchored audit evidence for customer support and compliance.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Per-tenant group-sequencing: assign a lightweight monotonic sequence token to group membership updates. SCIM write requests include the last-observed sequence; server rejects/queues out-of-order deltas and routes to an executor.
2) Joiner operation becomes an idempotent two-phase commit: (a) prepare - persist a "join intent" entry in a durable append-only store (WAL) with metadata (user_id, group_id, sequence, origin), (b) apply - attempt group link; on success mark as applied; on failure schedule exponential backoff retries. All steps append to the audit log to provide an immutable trail.
3) Repair/repair-playbook: provide a background reconciler that scans WAL tombstones and audit anchors to detect "intent not applied" and attempts deterministic repair. Repairs generate explainable audit events for admin review.
4) Admin reclaim flow: when a tenant admin marks an account as "reclaimed" or "soft-deactivated", the system will still honor join-intents for a configurable grace window and surface conflicts in the Admin Console with links to the audit evidence.
5) Observability & tracing: emit structured audit entries (immutable, sharded by tenant) and push a lightweight rewind index to S3 for forensics. Integrate trace IDs into console UI for one-click jump from a failed join to the exact WAL entry and PR/commit that changed the logic.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before release):
- Atomic joiner store implemented with append-only intents and a clear applied/failed state.
- Idempotent application logic: repeating the same intent (same origin+sequence) must be no-op after first success.
- Reconciler scan finds and repairs 99% of intents that failed due to transient infra errors within 24h in canary tenants (10 tenants).
- Audit anchors exist for every intent and are queryable from the Admin Console with tenant-level RBAC controls.
- No measurable regression (>5%) in average SCIM write latency for non-canonical tenants under baseline load.
- Migration plan documented and a rollback strategy exists (feature flag + canary + kill switch).

Notes on alternatives considered:
- Distributed locking per-group: rejected due to lock explosion and poor cross-region behavior under burst updates.
- Fully transactional DB join: rejected because it would require heavy schema change across sharded stores and rollback complexity for multi-tenant WAL.

Data retention and compliance:
- Intents and audit anchors retained for 365 days by default and configurable per-tenant.
- Audit entries include origin (IdP event id), request ID, IAM actor, and a non-repudiable checksum to support compliance requests.

Migration strategy:
- Implement behind feature-flag; enable for small set of internal tenants; run reconciler for 48h to measure false-positive repairs; expand to 10 canary customers; full rollout conditioned on observability metrics and security review.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (canary): enable on 10 tenants + reconciler off (monitor only)
- Week 2: enable reconciler for repair for canary tenants; monitor repair rate and latency impact
- Week 3: increase tenant coverage to 50; run security review and finalize console UI
- Week 4: full rollout behind opt-in with marketing/CS coordination
comments: 2025-11-05 - Spike completed: reproduced race condition between parallel SCIM group delta events when upstream sent concurrent adds to same group (IdP: Okta, peak delta). Reproducer attached.

2025-11-07 - Design proposal drafted. Concluded per-group sequencing + append-only intent store best tradeoff for cross-region reliability. Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ID/pages/SCIM-Atomic-Joiner-Design
2025-11-10 - Impl PR opened for intent WAL and apply worker: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1297 (WIP). Initial unit tests added for idempotency and sequence gating.
2025-11-13 - Security review checkpoint: discussed retention classification and checksum non-repudiation. SRE asked to validate S3 access patterns for audit anchors.
2025-11-16 - Demo to PM/Support: showed admin console link from a failed join to WAL entry; support asked for a one-click 'request repair' action - added to Acceptance Criteria.
2025-11-18 - Changed scope: include soft-deactivated reclaim grace window (configurable) per PM feedback. Updated estimates accordingly.
